faqs.q: Sec. 74-166. - Site assessments based on annexation or property acquisition initiated by owner.
faqs.a:
(a)
With regard to any property which the city may acquire through the initiative of the
               property owner, except as to transfer or sales from a public entity, the city shall
               require, prior to any such acquisition that a Phase I assessment be undertaken at
               the expense of the owner.
(1)
If as a result of the Phase I assessment, the city determines a Phase II assessment
               is necessary, the city shall require the owner to perform, at owner's expense, a Phase
               II assessment. If as a result of a Phase II assessment, the city determines that a
               Phase III assessment is necessary, the city may at its option negotiate the cost and
               timing of a Phase III assessment with the property owner, or terminate the acquisition
               of the property, or consummate the acquisition of the property after first taking
               into account the property's condition of environmental contamination.
(2)
The city may, as a condition of sale or other conveyance of property negotiated with
               another party, require, in form approved by the city attorney, a warranty and/or indemnification
               from the owner as to any condition of environmental contamination found on, or affecting,
               the property to be so acquired.
(b)
With regard to conveyance of property from a public entity to the city, the city may,
               at the city's option and expense, cause to be performed a Phase I assessment. If as
               a result of the Phase I assessment, the city determines that a Phase II assessment
               is necessary, the city may, at the city's expense, cause to be performed a Phase II
               assessment. If as a result of the Phase II assessment the city determines that a Phase
               III assessment is necessary, the city may at its option negotiate the cost and timing
               of a Phase III assessment with the public entity conveying the property, or terminate
               the acquisition of the property, or perform a Phase III assessment at the city's expense,
               or consummate the acquisition after taking into account the property's condition of
               environmental contamination.
(c)
With regard to any annexation to the city initiated by an owner of real property,
               except as provided in subsection (d) of this section, and as a condition of approval
               of such annexation, the owner, at the owner's expense shall have a Phase I assessment
               performed on all property to be annexed into the city. Such assessment shall be performed
               prior to filing of any annexation petition or any petition for an annexation election
               which includes the property assessed. The owner shall provide the results of such
               assessment to the city and the city shall determine the necessity of a Phase II assessment.
               If so required by the city, the owner shall, at the owner's expense, have performed
               a Phase II assessment which shall likewise be provided to the city. The city shall
               determine whether a Phase III assessment is necessary, and if so determined the owner
               shall, at the owner's expense, have a Phase III assessment performed prior to annexation
               by the city.
(1)
The city shall determine the adequacy of the site assessment performed by owner pursuant
               to this section and shall not be obliged to approve any petition for annexation on
               account of completion of a site assessment by owner. Nothing in this article shall
               limit the city's authority to approve or disapprove a proposed annexation as may be
               otherwise provided for in
chapter 74
,
Division 8-3-3
of the city Land Development Code or other applicable law.
(2)
The city may deny a petition for annexation based upon the failure of the owner of
               property to perform such site assessments as are required in this section. The city
               may deny a petition for annexation based solely upon a condition of environmental
               contamination revealed through a site assessment, which in the reasonable judgment
               of the city, poses a potential danger to the health, safety, or welfare of the citizens
               of the city or the persons who may work, reside or travel through or within the environmentally
               contaminated area.
(3)
As a condition of approval of annexation, the city may require remediation by the
               owner of any environmentally contaminated property belonging to an owner located within
               the proposed annexation area. Upon completion of remediation satisfactory to the city,
               the city may reconsider a previously denied petition for annexation. A petition for
               annexation may be placed in abeyance pending the results of a site assessment.
(4)
Approval of an annexation petition shall not act as a waiver of any requirement for
               remediation of hazardous substances previously established as a condition of annexation,
               or requirement established as part of an annexation agreement, or other assessment
               as may be required by this article. Nothing in this section shall prohibit the city
               from completing the annexation process, notwithstanding known conditions of environmental
               contamination, with or without remediation, if, as determined by the city manager,
               it is in the best interest of the city to complete the annexation process.
(5)
Approval of an annexation petition by the city, notwithstanding a condition of environmental
               contamination by hazardous substances, shall not constitute approval by the city of
               any development plan or plat submitted at the time such annexation petition is accepted,
               or at any time subsequent to such annexation. The city may require remediation of
               environmentally contaminated property prior to, or as a condition of, development
               or plat approval.
(6)
Any party seeking annexation into the city, or any party submitting a preliminary
               development plan or plat, shall be given notice of the provisions of this article
               following reasonable notice to the city community development department as to the
               respective party's intentions regarding annexation, platting, or development. It shall
               be the responsibility of the director of community development to provide notice to
               the party seeking platting, annexation, or development.
(7)
The city may, as a condition of annexation, require in form approved by the city attorney,
               an indemnification and/or warranty from owner as to any condition of environmental
               contamination by hazardous substances found on, or affecting, property annexed into
               the city.
(d)
With regard to an annexation initiated by an owner at the authorized request of the
               city, such annexation shall be treated, for purpose of environmental site assessment
               pursuant to this article, as if such annexation were initiated by the city. Accordingly,
               the responsibility for site assessment upon annexation shall be the responsibility
               of the city in the manner provided under
section 74-165
. For purposes of this subsection a request will be deemed authorized if authorized
               only by a majority of the city council.
(Code 1981, § 25-85; Ord. No. 3009, § 1, 10-4-1993; Ord. No.
4728
, § 23, 5-18-2020)
